title: The State of AI in Software Development: Data from 400+ Orgs — Justin Reock, DX
talk_summary: Justin Reock of DX presents aggregate research from ~200k engineers/400+ orgs on AI's real impact on software delivery: velocity gains are modest (median ~7.7% PR throughput), quality is volatile, PR sizes are ballooning, and change confidence is falling. The actionable core is that AI only helps if you attack the actual bottleneck and fix platform readiness (docs, modular code, non-flaky CI), with concrete org examples (Zapier, Morgan Stanley, Spotify) of agents applied to non-coding overhead.

takeaways.technique: Agent pre-review as system of record
takeaways.what_they_do: Zapier runs an agent on every PR that does superficial review first; its comments persist in the PR so the human reviewer sees what the agent already checked.
They argue token efficiency and agent effectiveness depend on platform hygiene: clear docs, modular code, reliable local CI, non-flaky tests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: reliable local CI and non-flaky test suites ... what's good for humans is also good for agents

takeaways.technique: PR size as a tracked guardrail
takeaways.what_they_do: They flag rising average PR size (44→72 lines) as a key quality risk driving review burden and lower change confidence; smaller PRs are easier to review and roll back.
takeaways.numbers: avg PR size 44→72 lines over ~1 year

takeaways.what_they_do: They measure token spend per use case and per cohort (junior vs senior) to find which use cases give efficient token spend and where steering/context is poor.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the more junior developers for the same use case will spend more tokens than a more senior developer on the same use case
takeaways.numbers: juniors spend more tokens for same use case; time savings roughly flat vs seniors

takeaways.what_they_do: Zapier uses an agent ecosystem for admin overhead (standup summaries) and Spotify uses an agent to assemble incident context from runbooks into comms channels.
takeaways.evidence_quote: They've reduced their standups by using a agent summaries ... to two times a week as opposed to five times a week
takeaways.numbers: standups 5x→2x/week; onboarding ~2 weeks vs >1 month benchmark

takeaways.what_they_do: They measure AI in three dimensions—utilization, impact on trusted metrics (PR cycle time, PR size, review pushback), and cost—and warn that gains off the bottleneck are worthless.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an hour saved on something that isn't the bottleneck is worthless
takeaways.numbers: median 7.7% PR-throughput gain; top performers ~70%, nobody hit 2x
